name: The account panel is the one DOM screen
summary: #acct is real markup rather than canvas because a canvas cannot raise a keyboard, be filled by a password manager, or offer a caret, selection, paste or autofill.
detail: The runtime binds it through acOn/runtimeListen, guards every access behind AC_DOM because harness stubs return non-elements, escapes every server-supplied name, clears acBody.innerHTML on close so no password lingers, and gives the panel the keyboard while it is open so typing does not reverse the comet. It appears only on the title screen.

name: Android Back as a boolean handshake
summary: The native bridge calls back() and minimizes the app only when it returns false; runtimeBack walks a fixed priority chain from account panel down to the title screen.
detail: Order: close the account panel, unpause, leave the lab to the powerup picker, pause a live run, return to the menu from any non-menu state, otherwise false. The bridge ignores the event entirely once disposed.

name: WebAudio ownership and gesture unlock
summary: Phaser’s sound manager is disabled with audio:{noAudio:true}; the runtime creates, resumes and gesture-unlocks its own AudioContext from forwarded input.
detail: ensureAudio creates the context lazily, resumes from suspended and from WebKit-only interrupted, and plays a one-sample buffer once because iOS will not truly start a context until sound has passed through it inside a gesture. Called from the top of pointerDown (7165), the Space/Enter keyDown branch (7451), unpauseGame (3332) and toggleMute (2905). Pause never suspends the context.

name: Phaser BLUR pauses, nothing resumes
summary: CosmoScene binds Phaser.Core.Events.BLUR to runtime.pause() and binds no FOCUS counterpart, so losing the window pauses the run and regaining it does not resume play.

name: __COSMO_BUILD__ crosses from Vite into the runtime
summary: vite.config.ts defines __COSMO_BUILD__ as the short git SHA on build and dev on serve; runtime.js reads it into BUILD and republishes it as window.COSMO_BUILD.
detail: buildId() shells out to git rev-parse --short=7 HEAD and falls back to COMMIT_REF or GITHUB_SHA truncated to seven characters, then to "dev". contracts.ts declares the global so TypeScript accepts it. The stamp now lands inside dist/assets/*.js, not dist/index.html.

name: The app shell DOM contract
summary: index.html supplies the elements the runtime binds by id — the #bg and #c canvases, the #safe inset probe and the #acct panel with its ac-* children — plus the module entry.
detail: html/body are overflow hidden with overscroll-behavior:none and touch-action:none so Phaser sees every pointer. #bg is z-index 0, #c is z-index 1 and transparent, #safe is a zero-size probe carrying env(safe-area-inset-*) padding that resize() reads with getComputedStyle. main.ts throws if #c is missing; CosmoScene throws if #bg or the 2D context is missing. The panel builds its remaining ac-* controls into #ac-body at render time.

name: Capacitor packages dist with fixed origins
summary: capacitor.config.ts bundles webDir dist with no server.url; Android serves https://localhost and iOS capacitor://localhost, and those origins scope every local record.
detail: appId app.cosmo.arcade, backgroundColor #030712 on both platforms, cleartext false, allowMixedContent false, iOS contentInset never with scrolling disabled and preferredContentMode mobile. tsconfig includes capacitor.config.ts in the typechecked set.

name: Frame loop ownership
summary: Phaser owns the frame loop: CosmoScene.update() calls runtime.step(delta) once per Phaser update, and the runtime schedules no frame of its own in production.
detail: runtimeStep converts ms to seconds and clamps to 0.05s, so a stalled tab cannot advance the simulation by a huge step. engineUpdates counts Phaser updates, steps counts runtime steps, and enginecheck asserts they track within one over 400ms.

name: The #bg WebGL canvas is host-supplied
summary: glInit renders the sky into host.background (#bg) rather than a canvas it owns, which is why teardown must not force a context loss on it.
detail: runtimeDisposeGpu calls WEBGL_lose_context only when the target is not GL or when no host background was supplied, because Phaser may hand the same #bg surface to a restarted scene. FX by contrast draws into a canvas the runtime created with document.createElement, so losing its context is free. #bg sits at z-index 0 under the transparent #c game canvas. Coverage is partial: fxcheck asserts GL.on comes up on a working GL and stays false with no GPU, and enginecheck asserts background.gpu with materialCount 3 in the built host — but no harness calls destroy, so the context-loss guard itself is asserted by nothing.

name: Haptics as an optional host callback
summary: Gameplay reaches haptics only through gameHaptic(kind, webPattern), which calls host.haptic when present and otherwise falls back to navigator.vibrate, swallowing every error.
detail: native.ts gates on hapticsEnabled, the bridge foreground flag and document.hidden, then rate-limits to one pulse per 65ms unless a higher priority supersedes (death 3, impact/reward 2, everything else 1). Web durations in ms: death 55, impact 35, reward 24, hop 12, tap/pickup 7. Native maps reward/death to Haptics.notification and the rest to impact Heavy/Medium/Light.

name: loadGameHtml assembles the virtual document
summary: Seven harnesses run against index.html with every script stripped, styles.css inlined into head, and the extracted runtime body injected as the single script before the closing body tag.
detail: check.mjs then asserts that result holds exactly one script block that parses, and that every id the body looks up with getElementById exists in the markup — a derived list, so #bg, #c and #safe cannot be renamed silently. check, curriculum, dropcheck, fxcheck, musiccheck, rendercheck and smoke use it; drawcheck takes loadGameSource instead, and enginecheck uses neither.

name: createCosmoRuntime(host)
summary: The single function where the Phaser/TypeScript shell hands the browser to the JavaScript runtime; RuntimeHost goes in, GameRuntime comes back.
detail: CosmoScene builds the host literal and calls createCosmoRuntime once per scene create. The runtime imports no Phaser and no Capacitor; the shell reaches the runtime only through the returned methods. src/game/runtime.d.ts is the only type Phaser ever sees of runtime.js.

name: Input ownership
summary: Phaser owns pointer and keyboard input; CosmoScene converts Phaser pointers back to client coordinates and forwards them as GamePointer, and the runtime binds no canvas listeners.
detail: CosmoScene.pointerEvent rebuilds clientX/clientY from the canvas bounding rect and this.scale dimensions, preserves the original pointerId when the DOM event has one, and turns a touchcancel/pointercancel POINTER_UP into pointerCancel. POINTER_UP_OUTSIDE shares the handler so a finger released off-canvas still ends the gesture.

name: externalLoop / externalLifecycle
summary: Two host booleans switch off the runtime’s entire pre-Phaser boot; leaving both Phaser and the legacy DOM loop/input active is the failure this boundary exists to prevent.
detail: externalLoop suppresses the standalone rAF loop (12324), the canvas pointer/contextmenu and window keydown listeners (7495), the window resize listener (665) and freshCheck (94). externalLifecycle suppresses the document visibilitychange listener (2888). Both are typed as the literal true in RuntimeHost, so a host cannot pass false and still typecheck. No static check asserts the guards survive; enginecheck only catches the symptom in a build that boots, by requiring frames and steps to track engineUpdates within one.

name: Foreground/background ownership
summary: src/platform/native.ts owns foreground detection by ANDing document visibility with Capacitor app state and publishing only on change; the runtime’s own visibility listener is disabled.
detail: installNativeBridge binds visibilitychange always and appStateChange/pause/resume only on native, seeds nativeActive from App.getState(), and fires callbacks.pause/resume solely on a transition. Its resume callback is deliberately wired to resizeToWindow, not runtime.resume, so returning from the background leaves the pause screen up.

name: Render ownership through OrbitDisplay
summary: The runtime draws inside Phaser’s Canvas render list: OrbitDisplay.renderCanvas calls camera.addToRenderList then runtime.render(), with no iframe and no CanvasTexture upload.
detail: runtimeRender snapshots the incoming 2D transform, globalAlpha and globalCompositeOperation, wraps draw() in try/finally and restores all three even when a frame throws, parking the first error on window.__drawErr. Phaser owns the canvas; the runtime must hand it back unchanged.

name: Resize and backing-store ownership
summary: Phaser owns the canvas backing store and CSS size; the runtime is told width/height in CSS pixels plus a dpr capped at 2, and never touches cv.width on the external path.
detail: resizeToWindow calls scale.resize(width*dpr, height*dpr), sets the canvas CSS size itself, then updateBounds() and displayScale.set() because Phaser.Scale.NONE will not — displayScale is what makes forwarded pointer coordinates land in the right place. Only then does it call runtime.resize(width, height, dpr).

name: The @runtime-body markers
summary: tools/lib/game-source.mjs cuts runtime.js between exactly one ordered pair of runtime-body markers, prefixes an empty host stub, and pads so stack line numbers stay aligned.
detail: A duplicated or reversed marker throws rather than producing a partial body. The empty host stub means the extracted body runs the legacy standalone path, which is what lets the VM harnesses drive the game through its real listeners. Body line N equals runtime.js line N for N from 8 onward; drawcheck reports violations by matching that path in the VM stack.

name: What a scene shutdown must release
summary: CosmoScene.shutdown removes native, window, BLUR and Phaser input listeners then calls runtime.destroy(), which drains every runtimeListen disposer, closes audio and releases both GPU chains.
detail: The scene sets disposed first so a queued resize is inert, disposes the native bridge (or disposes it on arrival if it resolves after shutdown), unbinds four pointer events plus keydown, then destroys the runtime and deletes window.COSMO_APP. OrbitDisplay is never explicitly destroyed; runtimeRender’s destroyed guard is what makes a late render harmless. No harness drives this path, so every claim here is read from source rather than asserted by a check.

name: window.COSMO_APP as the only read surface
summary: CosmoScene publishes window.COSMO_APP with engine, Phaser version and a snapshot() that merges runtime state with loopOwner, engineUpdates and the active scene count.
detail: It is installed at the end of create() and deleted in shutdown(). enginecheck observes the built app exclusively through it, including the background.gpu and materialCount fields. runtimeSnapshot also returns build and destroyed, which GameSnapshot does not declare and nothing reads.

name: Texture handover: BootScene cache to getTexture
summary: BootScene loads public/art/manifest.json into Phaser’s cache and CosmoScene exposes it as host.getTexture(key); every runtime art lookup treats null as draw the procedural version.
detail: BootScene rejects a key that is not [-\w]+ or a file that is not [-\w./]+.(png|webp|jpg) or contains "..", and starts Cosmo immediately when nothing queued. getTexture returns null unless the cached source is an HTMLImageElement or HTMLCanvasElement. The manifest holds 24 keys; the runtime asks for 20 — the 13-entry artKey table, four comet/UI literals and the three SKY_MATERIALS map keys — leaving 4 loaded and never requested.

name: window.storage is installed and removed by the runtime
summary: The cloud shim is added to window only while signed in and removed on sign-out; runtimeDestroy removes it only if window.storage is still the object this runtime installed.
detail: cloudInstallStorage strips the historical cometloop: prefix on both get and set and records the object in runtimeCloudStorage. Destroy also clears any pending cloud timer and flushes one final push before tearing down.

name: netlify/lib/accounts.mjs
summary: Passwordless identity: a name goes in, the server mints a randomUUID id and 32 random bytes as the key, and that key living in the browser is the login.
detail: No email exists in the system at all. cleanName collapses whitespace, slices to 12 and requires /^[A-Za-z0-9 _.\-]{1,12}$/. makeCode draws six characters from an alphabet with no O/0 and no I/1/L. Short is safe for a transfer code because it is single-use and expires; the key is long because it is the entire credential. The file states its own limit: this is a stable identity, not proof of who anyone is, and should be revisited before it is handed to strangers.

name: the checked-in Android project
summary: minSdk 24, compile and target SDK 36, AGP 8.13.0 on the Gradle 8.14.3 wrapper, one portrait singleTask activity and exactly one permission: INTERNET.
detail: applicationId and namespace are app.cosmo.arcade, versionCode 1, versionName 1.0, minifyEnabled false on release. The activity declares a configChanges list that includes orientation and screenSize, and there is an androidx FileProvider. docs/engine/native.md warns that large-screen Android can override the orientation restriction, so the layout must still fit a wide window. Release signing belongs to the owner and no keystore is in the repository.

name: .github/workflows/android.yml
summary: The only evidence in this repository that Cosmo compiles for Android: CI assembles a debug APK on every main push and uploads it as a 14-day artifact.
detail: Ubuntu runner under a 30-minute timeout: Node 24, Temurin JDK 21, android-actions/setup-android@v4, then sdkmanager for platform-tools, platforms;android-36 and build-tools;35.0.0. It runs npm ci, npm run build, the Capacitor CLI directly (node node_modules/@capacitor/cli/bin/capacitor sync android) and bash ./gradlew --no-daemon --stacktrace :app:assembleDebug from android/. "bash also works when a Windows checkout committed the wrapper as 0644."

name: the three Netlify functions
summary: auth.mjs at /api/auth, progress.mjs at /api/progress and scores.mjs at /api/scores — each declares its own path with export const config, and none of them ships in dist/.
detail: /api/auth is POST-only with an action of create, rename, code or link. /api/progress is GET to read the account document and PUT or POST to fold one in. /api/scores is GET for the board and POST to offer a run. Both blob stores that hold mutable state use consistency: strong. The client reaches them at an absolute origin so the Pages copy and both native WebViews hit the same service.

name: index.html
summary: A 43-line shell: the proprietary notice, meta and Open Graph tags, three canvases plus the account panel, and one module script — no game code at all.
detail: Body holds #bg (the WebGL sky canvas), #c (the Phaser game canvas), #safe (the safe-area probe) and #acct (the account panel, the only real DOM in a canvas game). The single entry is <script type="module" src="/src/main.ts">. The two absolute hrefs at :31-32 become ./manifest.webmanifest and ./apple-touch-icon.png in the built page under vite base "./", which is what lets the same bytes serve from the Pages subpath and from both Capacitor origins.

name: authenticate(req)
summary: The whole auth check: match Authorization: Bearer <id>.<key> against one regex, look the id up in the blob store, and compare the stored key.
detail: Nothing is decoded out of the token — the id is looked up, never believed. The comment names the failure that prevents: believing a self-asserted id, "the one that stays invisible until somebody tries it." A non-match returns null rather than throwing, and every caller turns that into a 401 with a CORS header attached.

name: netlify/functions/auth.mjs
summary: Four POST actions behind one path — create, rename, code and link — and the transfer code is what makes this a personal login rather than a per-device nickname.
detail: create and link are unauthenticated by necessity; rename and code require the bearer credential. Names are deliberately not unique: uniqueness would mean telling a stranger which names are taken, a rejection on the one screen that has to be frictionless, and an index to keep consistent. The code blob stores only {id, exp}; the key is read from the account when the code is spent, so a stolen code blob is not a stolen credential.

name: what leaves the leaderboard function
summary: GET rows carry only rank, name, score, level and at — no account id and no email ever leaves; a signed-in caller additionally gets their own standing.
detail: The name on a row resolves in order: what this run sent, then the account's own name, then whatever the row already held, then the literal PLAYER. The comment records the bug that ordering fixes — it read user.email.split('@')[0] until passwords were dropped and there stopped being an email, after which every submission without an explicit name landed on the board as PLAYER.

name: buildId() in vite.config.ts
summary: Four sources in order for the build stamp: the local git short SHA, then Netlify COMMIT_REF, then GitHub GITHUB_SHA, then the literal dev — and vite dev is always dev.
detail: execFileSync git rev-parse --short=7 HEAD with stderr ignored; the catch falls back to (COMMIT_REF || GITHUB_SHA || 'dev').slice(0,7). The define keys on command === 'build', so a development server stamps 'dev' even inside a git checkout. That is what makes BUILD==='dev' a usable guard for "this is not a deployed copy".

name: where the build stamp is visible
summary: Three surfaces expose BUILD: window.COSMO_BUILD, a faint bottom-right "build <sha>" line on the title screen only, and the build field of runtimeSnapshot().
detail: The title line is drawn at :12085, one row below the telemetry disclosure, and never during play. runtimeSnapshot().build is what window.COSMO_APP.snapshot() hands a harness or a console, so a person or a check can read the stamp without looking at pixels. Under the VM harnesses __COSMO_BUILD__ is undefined and BUILD is 'dev'; in the current artifact it is the seven-character short SHA.

name: Netlify cache headers
summary: The entry page is revalidated on every load and hashed Vite assets are immutable for a year — the header pair that replaced the in-page freshness check, on Netlify only.
detail: Two [[headers]] blocks give / and /index.html "no-cache, must-revalidate"; a third gives /assets/* "public, max-age=31536000, immutable", which is safe precisely because Vite hashes those filenames. GitHub Pages has no equivalent configuration anywhere in this repository, so the ten-minute entry-page cache that freshCheck was written against is still the Pages behaviour with nothing compensating for it.

name: rendercheck must have a browser in CI
summary: If pages.yml runs rendercheck without a playwright install step, check.mjs fails — otherwise the only check that looks at a pixel would report SKIP and success forever.
detail: rendercheck skips when no browser is present, which is right on a developer machine and fatal in the build. The install step is npx playwright install --with-deps chromium at pages.yml:29. enginecheck has the same dependency and handles it in its own file: it throws in CI and prints an explicit SKIP locally.

name: cloudSubmit(score, level, secs)
summary: The client refuses to offer a run to the board from the lab, on a zero score, or under five seconds — and swallows every failure, because a player who just died is owed the death screen.
detail: Called once, from die(). The five-second floor mirrors MIN_RUN_S on the server, so the two halves agree about what a run is. Nothing here is on the path of a run: a failure sets no error state and the next run offers the score again.

name: the link code is deleted before expiry is checked
summary: auth.mjs deletes the transfer code the moment it is presented, before it tests the expiry — because deleting only on the success path leaves every failure path as a retry loop.
detail: Order: normalise to six uppercase alphanumerics, load c/<code>, delete it unconditionally, then reject an expired code with 410 and a missing account with 404. A code that survives being presented can be presented again.

name: the CORS allowlist
summary: Seven exact origins, never a wildcard, and a preflight that answers 204 before any handler runs and without requiring auth.
detail: The list is the Netlify copy, the GitHub Pages copy, both bundled Capacitor WebView origins, and three localhost ports for development. cors() echoes the origin only on a match and sets vary: origin. The code says why * would be wrong: these endpoints carry a bearer key, and * is the shape of an account any page on the internet can read. preflight() must not require auth — the browser sends OPTIONS with no Authorization header by design, so an endpoint that 401s its own preflight is unreachable cross-origin.

name: package.json dependencies
summary: Seven runtime dependencies and five dev dependencies, all pinned to exact versions except @netlify/blobs, which is the only caret range in the file.
detail: Runtime: phaser 4.2.1, @capacitor/core|android|ios 8.5.1, @capacitor/app 8.1.1, @capacitor/haptics 8.0.2, @netlify/blobs ^8.1.0. Dev: @capacitor/cli 8.5.1, typescript 7.0.2, vite 8.2.2, playwright 1.56.1, @types/node 24.13.3. @netlify/blobs is used only by the server functions and never reaches dist/, which is why it is the one package whose exact bytes the shipped game does not depend on.

name: the dist/ completeness half
summary: The guard is not only "nothing extra": dist/ must contain index.html, at least one assets/*.js, and every single file that exists in public/.
detail: check.mjs:508-509 requires the entry page and a compiled bundle; :510-511 fails with "dist/ is missing public/<name>; rebuild the artifact" for any public file that did not survive the copy — a rebuild that dropped a sprite fails rather than shipping a game missing art. :512-514 re-reads the built dist/index.html and fails if Vite stripped the proprietary notice out of the HTML comment.

name: a document that names a constant must know its value
summary: check.mjs scans the runtime for SCREAMING_CASE numeric constants and fails any .md under docs/ (plus four root documents) that discusses one without naming its current value in the same paragraph.
detail: The rule is staleness, not agreement: history may stay ("0.42 was the retreat"), ignorance may not. Values are compared as numbers so prose may write 0.6 for 0.60. The window is the paragraph, not the file, because a long document satisfies any bare number by accident. The docs list is walked rather than hard-coded, so a new document is covered the day it is created; the walk fails if it finds fewer than eight documents.

name: tools/enginecheck.mjs
summary: The only harness that exercises the shipped artifact: it starts vite preview against dist/ on 127.0.0.1:4173 and drives the built Phaser app through real pointer and CDP touch input.
detail: It asserts dist/index.html exists first, then launches Chromium with SwiftShader ANGLE flags in a 390x844 touch context. It observes only window.COSMO_APP.snapshot() and browser errors — engine Phaser, loopOwner Phaser, sceneCount 1, LAUNCH by hit rect, a pointer tap reversing direction exactly once, a CDP swipe moving one ring inward, and steps/frames advancing once per Phaser update. It closes the browser and kills the preview in a finally block.

name: enginecheck aborts every off-origin request
summary: A route handler continues only GETs to its own preview origin and aborts everything else, so no account call and no telemetry POST can leave the check.
detail: The comment states both halves: the check needs only its own compiled assets, and "Rejected external requests must leave play functional." That is the one place in tools/ where the optional-cloud rule is exercised end to end against the real artifact — though it is exercised by denial, not by assertion: nothing checks that the game degraded correctly, only that no browser exception was raised.

name: stop at the first failing harness
summary: The runner exits on the first non-zero harness instead of continuing, because smoke, dropcheck and curriculum all drive the same front screens and would repeat one message three times.
detail: It prints the exit code or signal and the elapsed seconds before stopping. The reasoning is in the comment: the harnesses are not independent, so one broken screen fails three of them identically and only the first report is informative.

name: freshCheck() is disabled in the shipped host
summary: The play-link self-heal is fully implemented, documented and harness-asserted, and does not run in production: line 94 returns immediately because CosmoScene passes externalLoop: true.
detail: Its only call site is inside the if(!runtimeHost.externalLoop) block at :12324-12327. There is a second, independent reason it could not work if enabled: the parser at :103 is /const BUILD='([0-9a-f]{7})'/ and the shipped entry page is a shell whose only script is a module src — the stamp lives minified inside the bundle as a backtick literal, so neither the identifier nor the quoting survives. docs/engine/delivery.md documents the disabling as intended.

name: the full lane builds first
summary: Without --fast, all.mjs runs tsc --noEmit and vite build through process.execPath before the first harness, because rendercheck and enginecheck need a real dist/.
detail: Node is invoked directly on node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc and node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js rather than through npm, the same reason netlify/build.mjs gives: platform-specific npm shims cannot alter the build. --fast skips the build entirely, which is what makes the fast lane a few seconds instead of two minutes.

name: tools/all.mjs
summary: npm test in one file that holds no list of harnesses: it reads pages.yml, runs exactly the steps CI runs in CI order, and stops at the first failure.
detail: A list here would be a second copy of the CI list and the local runner would drift from the build — "all checks passed locally" while the pull request goes red. It is the complement of check.mjs: this proves the local run matches CI, check.mjs proves every harness in tools/ is wired into CI. Either alone leaves the other half open.

name: the one harness list
summary: Nine literal "- run: node tools/*.mjs" steps in pages.yml are the only list of harnesses; tools/all.mjs parses them and tools/check.mjs compares them against the tools/ directory.
detail: The comment above the block says why they must stay literal: "Keep explicit harness steps: tools/all.mjs reads this list." CI order is check, smoke, dropcheck, curriculum, musiccheck, fxcheck, drawcheck, rendercheck, enginecheck. all.mjs anchors its regex to a run: step so harness names in comments cannot be mistaken for steps; check.mjs compares the two sets in both directions.

name: every harness in tools/ runs in CI
summary: check.mjs builds the set of workflow run steps and the set of tools/*.mjs files (minus all.mjs, the runner) and fails on any difference in either direction.
detail: A harness in the tree that CI never runs "reads as coverage to anyone listing the directory, it passes when someone runs it by hand, and it never once runs on a pull request" — the same failure as a guard that cannot fail, which this repository has been bitten by twice. It also fails outright if no run steps are found at all, so a reshaped workflow cannot silently disarm the guard.

name: internalAsset(name)
summary: The deny half of the publish allowlist: four regexes that reject repository paths, agent documents, configuration files and any .md/.map/.pem/.key/.p12/.pfx/.toml/.yaml.
detail: Rejected path segments: .git*, .env*, node_modules, netlify, tools, docs, src. Rejected basenames: anything starting AGENTS, CLAUDE, README or MECHANICS. Rejected files: package.json, package-lock.json, netlify.toml, and any vite*/capacitor*/tsconfig* with a .ts, .js or .json extension. .map being on this list is the second lock behind vite.config.ts sourcemap:false, not the first.

name: the checked-in iOS project
summary: Swift Package Manager targeting iOS 15, capacitor-swift-pm pinned to exactly 8.5.1, portrait-only on iPhone and iPad with UIRequiresFullScreen — and no build evidence anywhere.
detail: CapacitorApp and CapacitorHaptics resolve from node_modules by relative path, so the iOS project cannot resolve without an npm ci first. iPad honours an orientation lock only in full screen, which is why UIRequiresFullScreen is true. There is no iOS workflow: docs/engine/native.md is explicit that generated project files are not evidence of a successful native build, and signing needs the owner's development team in Xcode on macOS.

name: keyMatches(a, b)
summary: A length-checked XOR accumulate instead of ===, written that way even though the threat is nil, because a === b in an auth path is the line that gets copied somewhere it matters.
detail: Returns false immediately on a type mismatch or a length mismatch, then ORs the character-code XOR across the whole string and compares the accumulator to zero.

name: the fast and full lanes
summary: Each harness declares its own lane in its first line; --fast runs the four static ones and skips the five that play whole games or launch a browser.
detail: all.mjs reads each harness file and defaults an undeclared one to full; check.mjs:383-389 fails the build if any harness declares no lane, so the default is a safety net rather than a resting place. --fast also refuses to run at all if it selected nothing. The comment beside the split still says "the quick four" against "the slow four" — written when there were eight; enginecheck.mjs later joined the full lane, so it is four against five. The assignment is correct; the prose beside it is off by one.

name: the last() merge rule is dead code
summary: records.mjs defines a last-write helper with a paragraph explaining it, and RULES never references it — muted and swipe use oneOf, name uses a bespoke validator.
detail: docs/engine/cloud.md's rule table still lists "last write | muted, swipe, name", which describes the behaviour correctly (all three are last-write-wins-if-valid) while naming a function nothing calls. The comment beside last() carries the argument worth keeping: applying max to a preference is how you build a mute that cannot be undone.

name: RULES and SYNCED_KEYS
summary: Twelve keys sync and nothing else: best, gl, runs, struggle, groove, hopped, landed, seen, seen2, muted, swipe and name, each with its own bounded rule.
detail: Keys are the bare name; the game stores everything under cometloop:<k> and the storage shim strips the prefix. merge() iterates SYNCED_KEYS only — a key not in the table is not synced, deliberately, because an unknown key is an unbounded write into a document the server hands back to every device on the account. cometloop:intro and cometloop:pid are written by the game and correctly never sync.

name: src/platform/native.ts
summary: Ninety-four lines with no dependency on scenes or gameplay: it takes three callbacks, folds document visibility together with Capacitor lifecycle events, and returns a disposer.
detail: publish() deduplicates transitions — active === wasActive returns early — so a WebView that fires both visibilitychange and appStateChange cannot double-pause. Plugin bindings go through Promise.allSettled, so a missing plugin cannot break startup, and only successfully bound listeners are collected for removal. Back falls through to App.minimizeApp() when the game does not consume it. CosmoScene installs it in create() and disposes it in shutdown(), with a race guard for a promise that resolves after teardown.

name: npm run native:sync
summary: Build the web product, then cap sync copies dist/ into both native projects and refreshes plugin references — it produces no APK, no binary and no signature.
detail: The copied web output is not in Git: android/.gitignore ignores app/src/main/assets/public and the generated capacitor config files, and ios/.gitignore ignores App/App/public and its config files. Gradle's wrapper is checked in; build output, local.properties, *.jks/*.keystore and keystore.properties are not. docs/invariants.md makes synchronizing after the final web build a rule.

name: netlify/build.mjs
summary: Eighteen lines: type-check, build, then assert dist/index.html exists — invoking Node directly so platform-specific npm shims cannot alter the build.
detail: Spawns process.execPath against node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit and then node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js build, exiting on the first non-zero status, and finishes with an access() on dist/index.html so a silent empty build cannot report success. It lives in netlify/ rather than tools/ because every file in tools/ is a CI harness and check.mjs enforces that; this asserts nothing about the game.

name: netlify.toml
summary: Netlify builds with node netlify/build.mjs, publishes the same dist/ directory Pages publishes, and deploys netlify/functions separately from the public game.
detail: NODE_VERSION is 24, matching the Pages workflow. The functions directory is never part of dist/, which is why the identical static artifact works on GitHub Pages and inside a Capacitor WebView with no functions behind it. The file's own header states the split: "Vite's built game is public. The bearer account-code service is optional."

name: package.json scripts
summary: Nine scripts: build is tsc --noEmit && vite build, test is tools/all.mjs, test:fast adds --fast, and native:sync is npm run build && cap sync.
detail: dev and preview both pin --host localhost. native:sync builds before it copies, which is the ordering docs/invariants.md makes a rule: synchronize after the final web build. native:android and native:ios only open the platform IDE projects; neither compiles anything.

name: .github/workflows/pages.yml
summary: The release path: one check job builds dist and runs nine harnesses, then uploads that exact directory as the Pages artifact for a deploy job that never rebuilds.
detail: Runs on push to main, on every pull request and on manual dispatch. SEED is github.run_number, so harness randomness rotates per run. Both the upload step and the deploy job are gated on refs/heads/main AND not a pull request, so a PR runs every check and publishes nothing. Concurrency cancels in-progress PR runs only; the pages deploy group is never cancelled.

name: netlify/lib/plausible.mjs
summary: The only judgement made about a submitted score: an integer inside a deliberately loose rate bound of 5000 + 1200 per second, on a run of at least five seconds.
detail: Split out of scores.mjs expressly so it can be tested without a network, a Netlify runtime or the blobs dependency — and then nothing was ever written to test it. The file works the arithmetic: sustained perfect play lands a couple of hundred points a second, so 1200/s is roughly five times what the game can pay. The bound exists to reject 9e9, never to adjudicate a good run, because a ceiling tuned close to real play would eventually call somebody's genuine best a forgery.

name: netlify/functions/progress.mjs
summary: The cloud save: GET returns the account document, PUT/POST folds a proposed one in with merge() and returns the merged result rather than an acknowledgement.
detail: Strong consistency is chosen explicitly because this is a read-modify-write two devices can race, and an eventual read would resurrect an old record as the base of the next merge. Returning the merged document is the round trip that teaches a device which posted a stale record about the better one it just lost to. The file header restates the rule: localStorage remains the real store; this is a copy that follows the account.

name: publicAsset(name)
summary: The allow half: exactly LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt, .nojekyll, and a fixed list of image, font, audio, video, json and webmanifest extensions.
detail: Extensions: png, jpe?g, webp, avif, gif, svg, ico, webmanifest, json, woff/woff2, ttf, otf, mp3, ogg, wav, m4a, aac, flac, mp4, webm. Nothing else passes. An .html file other than dist/index.html is not on the list, and neither is a .js or .css outside dist/assets/ — so a stray page or a hand-written script cannot become a URL.

name: public/
summary: The 32 files Vite copies verbatim into dist/: 25 art files, three icons, og.png, the webmanifest, LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt.
detail: As read at commit 01a3a25: 24 sprites plus art/manifest.json under public/art/, icon-192.png, icon-512.png, apple-touch-icon.png, og.png, manifest.webmanifest, LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. The ten opaque world plates under public/art/worlds/ were deleted in this commit range and the licence file now says they are kept outside the game as references. dist/ is a build product and is gitignored, so it is not part of the checked-in inventory.

name: what may become a public URL
summary: One deny-then-allow predicate pair, applied to both public/ and dist/, decides every file that can be served — plus a symlink ban and a completeness check in the same block.
detail: assetFiles() walks a tree and fails on any symlink (a published tree that can point outside itself is directory traversal waiting to be served). Every public/ file must satisfy publicAsset and fail internalAsset. dist/ additionally permits index.html and assets/<hash>.js|.css. The dist scan tolerates ENOENT so the fast lane may run before a build; enginecheck is the harness that requires a real dist.

name: netlify/lib/records.mjs
summary: The server folds a proposed document into the stored one with per-key rules — max, sticky, union, oneOf and a bespoke name — so two devices commute and a stale phone cannot erase a record.
detail: Once a record is monotonic, order stops mattering, which is what makes an offline device safe to sync days later. It removes a class of tampering for free: a client that posts best:0 cannot lower anything, and the clamps stop "up" meaning 9e9. sticky is justified separately — forgetting "this human has once done X" would replay a once-ever tutorial at somebody already taught.

name: every harness is named in docs/harnesses.md
summary: A whole-file substring search requires each harness filename to appear in the one routing document, because the document claimed this guard existed years before it did.
detail: docs/harnesses.md said "Adding a harness is three edits, and check.mjs fails until all three are made" while only two were enforced. It had already failed: rendercheck.mjs, the only harness that reads a pixel, was missing from both docs/harnesses.md and README.md while both asserted fxcheck was the only render-path check. Whole-file rather than near-the-name is deliberate — a filename cannot appear in prose by accident. README.md was dropped from the routing list after both copies of the table went stale together.

name: netlify/functions/scores.mjs
summary: One blob holding the top 100, 25 rows returned by default, one row per player, a ten-second cooldown, and no pretence of being unforgeable.
detail: The whole game is delivered to the browser and the repository is public, so it rejects the impossible and the automated instead: you must be signed in, the score must pass plausible.mjs, and a resubmission that does not beat your own stored score returns improved:false rather than adding a row. Two open items are written down rather than hidden — one blob means last write wins and two people finishing in the same second can drop an entry, and closing forgery would need server-side replay the game cannot support.

name: a seeded harness must print its seed
summary: Any harness containing seededMath must also contain console.log(seedLine( — because CI rotates SEED per run and a failure without its seed cannot be reproduced.
detail: The guard exists because curriculum, dropcheck, fxcheck and musiccheck all imported seedLine and never called it, for four sessions, while CLAUDE.md and docs/harnesses.md both stated the opposite in as many words. "The claim was prose; nothing executed it. It is an assertion now." CI supplies SEED as github.run_number, so coverage moves every run.

name: the app-shell tripwires
summary: Three assertions on index.html: it has a module script entry, it does NOT contain an inline script declaring const G =, and it carries both "copyright" and "all rights reserved".
detail: The const G tripwire is aimed at a real prior shape of this project — index.html holding a second copy of the canonical game beside src/game/runtime.js. The notice is checked twice, once in the source shell and again in the built dist/index.html (check.mjs:512-514), because Vite could strip an HTML comment. The notice currently lives in the comment block at index.html:2-9 and survives the build.

name: check job uploads, deploy job publishes
summary: The artifact handed to Pages is the dist that the nine harnesses just passed against; the deploy job contains no checkout, no npm and no build step.
detail: The comment above the upload step states the rule: "Ship the exact bundle that passed every check. Do not rebuild in deploy." The deploy job only runs actions/configure-pages@v5 and actions/deploy-pages@v4. A rebuild there would publish bytes nothing had checked, and the build stamp would still name the same commit — so the failure would be invisible.

name: the collection disclosure line
summary: The title screen prints "Anonymous play stats collected" whenever POSTHOG_KEY is set, one line above the build stamp in the same faint footer band.
detail: It is drawn only in the menu state, never during play, and it is keyed on the constant rather than on TELE_OK — so a local copy that sends nothing still says so, which is the honest direction for that mismatch to fall.

name: the event inventory
summary: Seventeen distinct event names across eighteen call sites; run_ended is the wide one and swipe_mode_chosen is the only name that fires from two places.
detail: run_ended carries roughly forty properties covering score, records, pacing, teaching outcomes and gesture misread rate. pauses/paused_seconds and chorus_entries/chorus_bars ride both run_ended and level_cleared on the same per-level scale, because startGame() re-baselines the counters at every level boundary — without the pair on both, a pause taken on level 1 of a run that died on level 4 was recorded nowhere at all.

name: the three gates before anything is sent
summary: TELE_OK silences file:// and every localhost form, the lab is suppressed at the single choke point, and the whole of track() is wrapped so a telemetry failure can never interrupt play.
detail: TELE_OK is false when protocol is file: or the hostname starts localhost, 127. or 0.0.0.0 — so development and every harness send nothing at all. The lab gate lets exactly one name through, powerup_lab_started. Suppressing at the choke point rather than tagging a lab_run property means a later session's new event inherits the silence for free, and blackhole_entered keeps meaning "a player met one in a real run".

name: the five properties on every event
summary: $process_person_profile:false, swipe_mode, play_mode, $current_url on every event, plus account_id only when signed in.
detail: play_mode is deliberately not called mode: swipe_mode_chosen has always carried the swipe rule under mode, and reusing the name would rewrite what every historical row of that event says. One name per thing; retire, never reuse. $process_person_profile:false keeps a signed-in player's events anonymous events that happen to carry a stable key.

name: what identifies a player to PostHog
summary: One random id per device in localStorage under cometloop:pid, falling back to a per-visit id in private mode, plus an opaque account uuid on signed-in devices only.
detail: TELE_ID is 'p' + a base-36 random + a base-36 timestamp. No autocapture, no session recording, no cookies, no names, no email — there is no email anywhere in the system. TELE_ACCT is stamped by cloudSaveTok and is the join between the two halves of the data: Netlify holds records and the board keyed by account, PostHog holds the funnel keyed by the anonymous device id. A device that never signs in is unchanged.

name: the telemetry transport
summary: Plain POSTs to PostHog with no SDK and no third-party script: sendBeacon first so a death recorded as the tab closes still gets out, keepalive fetch as the fallback, all inside one try/catch.
detail: The body is a JSON string, which goes out as text/plain — a CORS simple request, so there is no preflight for sendBeacon to fail on. Nothing to load means no load order to get wrong and no loader to fail silently. The embedded key is a PostHog project token: write-only by design, safe in a public file. A blocked or dead network is silence; telemetry is a listener, never a dependency.

name: public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt
summary: The 162-line notice that ships with the game: the supplied Gemini artwork provenance plus the MIT texts for Phaser 4.2.1 and the five Capacitor packages.
detail: Covers phaser 4.2.1 (Richard Davey, Phaser Studio), @capacitor/core, /android and /ios 8.5.1, @capacitor/app 8.1.1 and @capacitor/haptics 8.0.2 (Drifty Co.). It deliberately does not list vite, typescript, playwright or @netlify/blobs — none of them are distributed inside dist/. The artwork section records supplied provenance without inferring a third-party artwork licence, and now states that only the 24 transparent sprites are distributed.

name: the pages.yml step parser
summary: One anchored regex extracts the harness steps from the workflow, and a floor of two parsed steps fails the runner rather than letting it silently run nothing.
detail: The pattern is /^[ \t]*-[ \t]+run:[ \t]+node[ \t]+(tools\/[\w.-]+\.mjs)[ \t]*$/gm. Anchoring to a run: step is deliberate — harness filenames appear in this file's own comments and in the workflow's comments, and an unanchored match would run those. The floor is a floor rather than an exact count so adding a check need not edit this file: "a runner that silently runs nothing reports success."

name: applySect(s) and applyLevelMusic()
summary: The only writer of the live CH and ARP tables; applyLevelMusic additionally rescales PENT by the level key.
detail: applySect(0) is the verse, applySect(1) the chorus; it copies a row set from PROG/PROGB and ARPL/ARPBL. It touches tables, never oscillators — the pad retunes at the next bar line. applyLevelMusic is called from startGame and always opens on the verse.

name: armDrop(why,src)
summary: Arms the next Starfall, or banks it into MU.pend when the music is busy, and plays the earn stab either way.
detail: Called from build (1324), from bedTick when a banked earning can finally fire (2751), and re-banked by endSection and startBlackHole. An earning is never discarded — the cooldown only stops two sections overlapping.

name: artifactSprite
summary: Bakes one cached sprite per hazard/orb kind, preferring the host texture named by a thirteen-entry artKey table and falling back to the procedural vector artwork.
detail: The cache key is u + ":" + DPR, so a resize or dpr change rebakes everything. This is one of six sites that read the raw host parameter rather than the null-guarded runtimeHost.

name: bedTick(dt)
summary: The only writer of BED.g and of the pad voice weights, and the function that calls musicTick.
detail: Called unconditionally from update. Sets the pad level, the pad filter cutoff, A.band, the four voice weights from orbit pressure, drains BEATQ and DROPQ, decays PLAY.heat, and enforces MU.payEnd as the section deadline. Nothing else may write BED.g.

name: beep(f,d,type,g,slide,when,pan,wet)
summary: The sound-effect voice, kept at its original signature because thirty call sites depend on it; applies the black hole redshift.
detail: Routes to A.world, so it is audible through the band duck. `when` schedules on the audio clock rather than setTimeout. Inside black-hole phase 2 it multiplies f and slide by a squared curve reaching 2^(-5/12); phases 1 and 3 keep their pitch so the entry and exit cues stay recognisable.

name: bhTick(dt)
summary: Advances the black hole through its four phases and is the only writer of RADII.
detail: Called from update whenever the state is playing OR the mode is active, so it can complete across a death. Phase 2 opens the fourth ring and pulls the comet inward every BH_PULL seconds; the closing phase withdraws every entity from the vanishing lane before its radius reaches zero.

name: build(amount,src)
summary: The Starfall meter. Rejects every source but a completed star-fed orbit, then counts to dropNeed and arms.
detail: Signature build(amount, src). The guard at 1322 — src!=="orbit" || amount<0.04 — makes five of the six call sites no-ops: the per-second tick, the ember pickup, the hop, the tight tap and the near-miss all pass an amount or a source that is rejected. Only the 0.043 orbit call at 8404 survives.

name: buildBed()
summary: Starts the four continuously-running detuned pad voices, generates the shared noise buffer, and initialises MU.
detail: Signature buildBed(). Called only from the last line of buildBus. The pad is eight oscillators (four voices x two detuned unisons) retuned by setTargetAtTime, never restarted. NOISE is 1.5 s so the drop riser's 1.73 s sweep does not loop audibly.

name: buildBus()
summary: Builds the WebAudio graph once and assigns A; idempotent, and calls buildBed at the end.
detail: Signature buildBus(). Returns early if A already exists or AC is null. Node names that matter downstream: A.world (SFX), A.bed (music), A.hole (the drop silence), A.pump (sidechain), A.band, A.perf (the player, bypassing hole and bedDuck), A.dly (dotted-eighth dub delay), A.send (reverb).

name: chTone(ix) and chI(bar)
summary: Resolves an index into the chord sounding right now — 0-3 walk the voicing, each block of four an octave up.
detail: chI applies the chorus rotation CHOFF so a chorus can open off-tonic while CH[0] stays the tonic chord twenty-five readers assume. Everything the player triggers speaks through chTone, which is why a tap is harmonically correct by construction rather than by luck.

name: window.COSMO_APP
summary: The debug/harness global the scene publishes: engine name, Phaser.VERSION and a snapshot function; declared on Window in contracts.ts and deleted on shutdown.

name: CosmoScene.pointerEvent
summary: Rebuilds a GamePointer from a Phaser pointer: the original DOM pointerId when available, and client coordinates recovered through the canvas rect and this.scale dimensions.
detail: clientX = rect.left + pointer.x * rect.width / scale.width. Phaser reports pointer coordinates in backing-store space and the runtime works in CSS pixels, so this division is the counterpart of resizeToWindow’s displayScale.set. preventDefault is forwarded only when the underlying event is cancelable.

name: CosmoScene.resizeToWindow
summary: Resizes Phaser to window*dpr, sets the canvas CSS size, updates bounds and displayScale by hand because Phaser.Scale.NONE will not, and finally tells the runtime in CSS pixels.
detail: Bound to window resize, visualViewport resize and the native bridge resume callback. It returns immediately once the scene is disposed or before the runtime exists.

name: createCosmoRuntime
summary: The runtime’s only export: it evaluates the whole 12,000-line body as one closure over host and returns the GameRuntime object the scene drives.
detail: Its first act is runtimeHost = typeof host !== "undefined" && host ? host : {}, so a null host cannot crash a property read. Importing the module never schedules a frame; only the no-host path starts one.

name: cueTone(fn)
summary: Hands a callback the delay that lands its notes on the next free sixteenth, so the game's replies form a note run instead of a cloud.
detail: Signature cueTone(fn) where fn receives a delay in seconds relative to AC.currentTime. Falls through to fn(0) when there is no scheduler. A slot already taken cascades one sixteenth, capped a beat out. Twenty-four call sites: embers, orbits, shields, hops, milestones, lessons, the finale.

name: currentWakeUpdate(dt)
summary: Advances the thirty-six dust strands and decays the shared G.currentFlow envelopes every frame.
detail: Called with the presentation delta from update (7917 for the intro, 8257 for play). It emits new strands only while the reversal is committed (G.revPend<=0), so a speculative tap leaves no wake to roll back. The envelopes it maintains are read by audio, by the shader and by the panner.

name: die()
summary: Ends the run, writes the records, arms the death coaching and the killer-lesson re-offer, and fires run_ended.
detail: Called from updateSpikes and from a failed black-hole escape. Every persisted write is guarded by !LAB.on; the deepest-level record additionally requires G.startLevel===1 so a picked level cannot forge a climb.

name: dl()
summary: The difficulty clock in difficulty-seconds: the level floor plus a re-run of the gentle opening ramp, scaled by the mode.
detail: Returns 0 during the intro and LAB_DL in the lab. Everything that presses on the player keys off this one number, which is why the lab pins it and a future mode scales it rather than trimming six terms separately.

name: draw()
summary: The world render pass, in one fixed order, wrapped by runtimeRender's transform repair.
detail: Resets the transform, alpha and composite mode at the top because a thrown frame otherwise poisons every later one. Sets paX/paY (10696) before anything calls posAt. Ends by drawing the HUD and the five controls, with the pause blackout last so it covers them.

name: drawBloom()
summary: Rebuilds the bright buffer from every light in the scene and composites the halo, choosing the GPU or the disc path once per frame.
detail: bloomHalo=!FX.on is decided before the dot loop so the two paths can never both draw. The composite resets to setTransform(DPR,...) because the bright pass draws without the camera dolly — the mismatch was a visible wobble on every light.

name: drawHUD()
summary: The lesson veil plus the seven-way state dispatch that also publishes every hit rectangle the input handler reads.
detail: Branches: playing (drawRunHUD), lvend, swipesel, menu, levelsel, powersel, else the death screen. There is no paused branch — pause is a flag and the run stays "playing", which is why drawPausePanel is drawn separately after the HUD.

name: duckBed(amount,rel)
summary: Dips A.bed and writes its own recovery in the same call; refuses to fire inside the drop hush.
detail: Six call sites: black-hole entry, the drum break, the milestone orbit, soundImpact, levelComplete and die. The hush guard at 2846 is currently unreachable because schedulePreDrop has no caller.

name: effRing() and curR()
summary: The ring collision runs on during a hop (switching at the halfway point) and the eased radius the comet is drawn at.
detail: curR uses ease-out-back with a 6u clamp so the comet cannot visibly leave the track band; under reduced motion it falls back to smoothstep. Collision is on ring indices only — the two never disagree because effRing is the single source.

name: endSection()
summary: Clears every interrupted musical phrase through one path, banks an unpaid earning, and restores A.hole and A.pump.
detail: Thirteen call sites. Banks only while the state is still playing — death and menu start clean. Always lands back on the verse. This is the belt-and-braces restore, not the mechanism: every duck is supposed to write its own undo.

name: ensureAudio
summary: Creates the AudioContext on demand, resumes it from suspended or WebKit-only interrupted, plays a one-sample buffer once to satisfy iOS gesture unlock, then builds the bus.
detail: Everything is inside one try/catch, so a device with no WebAudio simply plays a silent game. It is reached from forwarded input, from unpause and from the mute toggle — never from a timer.

name: farFromAll(a,ring,minP,minSpike,minStar,behind)
summary: The placement predicate: clear of the player along the heading, and clear of every spike, star and orb on that ring.
detail: With behind>0 the player term is asymmetric — full clearance ahead, only `behind` radians of pad behind; with behind falsy it is the old symmetric read, which is what stars, orbs and gate segments still use. Distances are radians and callers pass sep(ring,k) so the clearance is correct on every ring.

name: fireDrop(t)
summary: Lands the payoff: sets MU.pay, the cooldown, the crown ring and the flavour, plays the impact stack, and queues the visual.
detail: Called from musicStep on an armed even eighth. Every pitch is an interval over CH[0][0] so the drop is in the level key. It deliberately schedules no kick at t — payoffStep's bar 0 fires one at the same instant. DROPQ.push(t) is what makes the picture wait for the sound.

name: firstMeet(type)
summary: Shows a mechanic's once-per-device lesson, or defers it without spending it.
detail: Eleven guards, each of which returns WITHOUT setting G.seen so the next encounter re-offers. Sets G.teach (2.8 s), G.teachKind="see", G.teachType and G.teachHint, persists the seen set, and plays cueLesson. Never runs in the lab, and soft lessons wait for the red lesson to land first.

name: freshCheck
summary: The self-refresh check that redirected a stale page to a newer build; still present in runtime.js but unreachable in every shipping configuration and no longer matching what Vite emits.
detail: Its only call site sits inside if(!runtimeHost.externalLoop), and its own first line returns when externalLoop is set, so production never runs it. On the harness path BUILD is "dev" and line 96 returns. Its regex looks for a literal const BUILD= assignment in the first 8KB of index.html; dist/index.html contains no such string because Vite emits the runtime into dist/assets/*.js.

name: frozen()
summary: The single predicate that says the world is not running — read by update and by both input handlers so they can never disagree.
detail: Returns PAUSE.on || PAUSE.resumeT>0, so it covers both the panel and the three-second count-in. canPause (3296) is its complement plus the cooldown.

name: fxRender(srcCanvas,bw,bh)
summary: Blurs the bright buffer at two levels on the GPU and composites them with chromatic spread; returns false on any failure.
detail: Must check isContextLost explicitly: a lost WebGL context does not throw, it silently no-ops, and a quiet success would composite an empty canvas with no way back. A failure is permanent for the session.

name: G
summary: The one mutable state object — 75 lines of fields covering clocks, run counters, position, reward states, entities and draw envelopes.
detail: Declared after every function that reads it, and immediately followed by loadPrefs(). G.t is the measured clock and G.vt the presentation clock; G.tsCur is the eased scale between them. G.seen/G.seen2 are the persisted taught sets; G.carry* are the level-boundary handoff.

name: GamePointer
summary: The normalized pointer the runtime accepts: pointerId, clientX, clientY, a type string and preventDefault — deliberately not a DOM event.
detail: runtimePointerEvent inside the runtime re-normalizes whatever arrives, defaulting pointerId from event.id and coordinates from event.x/y, so both the Phaser adapter and the harnesses hand-built objects work.

name: GameRuntime
summary: The methods the shell may call: step, render, resize, the four pointer entries, keyDown, pause, resume, back, snapshot and destroy.
detail: back() returns boolean because Android Back needs to know whether the app should minimize. Everything else returns void. resize takes width, height and dpr rather than reading the window.

name: GameSnapshot
summary: The read-only view the host publishes: state, introStage, ringIndex, direction, score, level, paused, viewport, menuRects, introSkipRect, frames, steps, background, reward and three host-added fields.
detail: loopOwner, sceneCount and engineUpdates are optional because only CosmoScene fills them; the runtime cannot know them. background {gpu, materialCount} and reward {orbits, starfall, wave} are required and come from the runtime. menuRects and introSkipRect are copied, not shared, so a reader cannot mutate game state through the snapshot.

name: glInit
summary: Brings up the WebGL sky on host.background, falling back to getElementById("bg"), and returns false on any failure so the 2D fallback sky draws instead.
detail: Every failure path is silent by design: no context, no shader compile, no program link, or a thrown exception all return false. tools/check.mjs derives its required-id list from the source precisely because that silence once hid the starfield disappearing for every visitor.

name: glRender(dt)
summary: Uploads twenty uniforms and three optional textures, then draws the whole background as one triangle.
detail: Called from draw when GL.on; any throw sets GL.on=false permanently and the CPU sky takes over on the next frame. Its uniforms carry the arena radii, the comet position, the orbit flow envelopes and the starfall progress, which is how the sky answers play rather than a timer.

name: gridNear()
summary: Returns the nearest sixteenth grid point, which may sit slightly in the past — the caller clamps.
detail: Returns AC.currentTime+0.015 when there is no schedule. Deliberately not clamped internally: a clamped now+12ms would make every front-half tap a unique timestamp and defeat performerHit's one-note-per-slot dedupe.

name: haptic
summary: One bounded pulse per event with a 65ms gate a higher-priority impact may supersede; silent when disabled, backgrounded or hidden, and never throwing on unsupported hardware.

name: hintText()
summary: Returns the one line of standing guidance for right now, or null; each line retires on the action it teaches.
detail: Suppressed entirely outside play, in the intro, in the lab, inside a black hole and during the finale. A live first-encounter lesson outranks it. Every line either quotes MEET or is generated by swipeWords, so the ladder cannot describe a control scheme the build does not have.

name: hop(step)
summary: Changes ring by step, or bumps and still plays a note when there is nowhere to go.
detail: step is -1 outward, +1 inward. Sets G.hopFrom/hopFromI/ringI/hopP, marks the wake, clears nearby red under slipstream, and calls performerHit with the ARRIVING ring. Refuses while a hop is in flight (G.hopP<1).

name: installNativeBridge
summary: Binds visibility plus Capacitor appStateChange/pause/resume/backButton once, publishes only on a real foreground change, and returns a disposer that removes exactly its own listeners.
detail: Promise.allSettled around the four addListener calls means one failing plugin cannot prevent the others binding; only fulfilled handles are stored for removal. If the document is already hidden at bind time it calls pause immediately. App.getState seeds nativeActive, with visibility as the fallback if it throws.

name: judgeTiming(x,y)
summary: Scores a tap on three tiers against a learned device bias and returns the resulting ON BEAT chain value.
detail: Returns G.groove (0-8). Only performerHit calls it. The quarter anchor is MU.next plus half a beat when MU.step is odd; anchoring it wrong judges the offbeat, which musiccheck catches. The steadyhand upgrade widens the window from 0.032 to 0.045.

name: loadGameHtml
summary: Builds the harnesses virtual document: index.html with all scripts stripped, styles.css inlined into head, and the extracted runtime body injected before the closing body tag.
detail: It throws if the shell has no closing body tag to inject into, so a restructured app shell fails loudly instead of producing a document with no game in it.

name: loadGameSource
summary: Reads runtime.js, demands exactly one ordered pair of runtime-body markers, and returns the body prefixed with an empty host stub and padded so line numbers match the file.

name: MEET
summary: One sentence and one glyph per teachable idea — the exact string the banner sub and the death coach also print.
detail: Keys are formation types plus orb ids plus orbit, lapcost, music, beat and combo. `soft:1` means the lesson shows without slow motion. Changing a line here means changing its tier row and MECHANICS.md in the same commit.

name: musicStep(i,t,k)
summary: Schedules one eighth of the arrangement at audio time t, with i the step index in the 32-step loop and k the normalised difficulty.
detail: The dispatch order is the contract: section seam (i===0 only), chord retune, black hole, payoff, armed fire, star dive, then the ordinary arrangement. Everything below a `return` in this function is silent for that eighth. k is min(1, dl()/150).

name: musicTick()
summary: Walks MU.step forward until the schedule reaches 160 ms ahead of the audio clock, at most sixteen steps per call.
detail: Called only from bedTick. Detects a gap greater than 0.4 s and abandons the section rather than replaying it compressed. When not playing it ends any live section and zeroes MU.next.

name: note(f,t,dur,type,g,cut,pan,bus,echo)
summary: The one-shot musical voice: oscillator into a closing lowpass, optional pan, optional dub send, routed to A.bed unless a bus is named.
detail: Nine positional arguments; only the first five are ever required. Passing A.perf as `bus` is what puts a sound on the player's own path — drier (0.28 send instead of 0.5) and outside the drop's hole. Roughly a hundred call sites. Silent when muted or before the bus exists.

name: novaConvert(s,toRing)
summary: Turns one shard into embers on the player's ring, spaced along the lane, and plays the next degree of an ascending sixteenth run.
detail: Called by the nova front, the hypernova plough and the slipstream clear. The spacing walk steps 0.36 rad in the direction of travel until it finds room, so a converted wall reads as a necklace rather than a pile. RICH NOVA doubles the yield through the same walk.

name: OrbitDisplay
summary: A bare Phaser GameObject whose only job is renderCanvas: it adds itself to the camera render list and calls runtime.render() in place.
detail: This is what replaces the old iframe and the per-frame CanvasTexture upload. It keeps its own reference to the runtime, so it can outlive CosmoScene.runtime being cleared; runtimeRender’s destroyed guard covers that.

name: orbitMusicState()
summary: Reduces the live orbit and the gesture wake to {active, q, turn, hop, radial, dir, pressure} for the pad and the chorus colour.
detail: Reads G.currentFlow, G.lapEmbers, G.lapAcc and G.lapStreak. Inactive during hypernova, overdrive, an armed or live payoff, a black hole, the finale, a starfall release and any freeze. Consumed by musicStep (1796) and bedTick (2733).

name: payoffStep(t,ch,k)
summary: Plays one eighth of the eight-bar payoff section, including the sidechain pump and the per-level hook.
detail: n = PAY - MU.pay gives the position; pb is the bar, ps the eighth. Bars 2, 3 and 6 are the answering phrase (ANSWERL); bar 7 is the written descent. MU.crown raises the richness, MU.flavor colours the texture, MU.payN alternates the second ending.

name: performerHit(kind,dir,ring)
summary: Plays the player's own instrument for a tap or a hop, on the grid, on A.perf, as a chord tone of the current bar.
detail: kind is "rev" or "hop"; ring is the ring being ARRIVED at. Returns nothing. Refuses while frozen, outside play, with no audio, or inside a black hole. It also drives PLAY.heat (+0.26 per input) which is the engagement term the whole arrangement opens on.

name: pickType()
summary: Chooses the next formation: the newest unmet shape insists until its lesson lands, otherwise a rank-weighted draw.
detail: Returns a formation type string. Both loops carry the same exclusions by duplication — twins capped at two pairs past dl 340, one wall at a time, no gate beside a saucer, dive and funnel need two rings. The rank weighting is identity below dl 340, so levels 1-3 are untouched by construction.

name: reverse(silent) and reverseFX()
summary: Flips direction immediately and, when silent, defers every effect by REV_FX so a gesture that becomes a swipe can roll it back.
detail: reverse zeroes lapAcc and lapStreak but banks the travelled arc into G.skyW first, so tapping still buys the journey. reverseFX plays the sound, the ripple, the flip and the performer note; commitReverseFX fires it at lift.

name: RINGS
summary: Four rows of wave, cutoff multiple, filter lift, sub level and tint — each ring is an instrument.
detail: Read by musicStep (kit stacking), bedTick (the lift term in the pad cutoff), performerHit (the player voice) and the rail draw (the tint). The fourth row is the accretion ring and is only reachable inside a black hole; it is violet because it belongs to the mode, not to the ladder.

name: runtimeBack
summary: The Android Back chain: close the account panel, unpause, leave the lab, pause a live run, return to the menu, else return false so the app minimizes.

name: runtimeDestroy
summary: Idempotent teardown: sets runtimeDestroyed, cancels any standalone frame, drains every listener disposer, flushes the cloud push, closes audio, releases both GPU chains and empties the sprite caches.

name: runtimeDisposeGpu
summary: Deletes a GL target’s material and blank textures, framebuffers, buffer, shaders and programs, and forces a context loss only when the surface is not the host-supplied background.
detail: Every GL deletion sits inside one try/catch — a teardown that throws would leave the scene half-destroyed, which is worse than a leaked buffer — and the field resets after the catch always run. No harness calls it; this record is read from source, not asserted by a check.

name: RuntimeHost
summary: The typed record the shell hands in: canvas, context, background, width, height, dpr, externalLoop, externalLifecycle, and optional native, haptic and getTexture.
detail: externalLoop and externalLifecycle are typed as the literal true, not boolean, so no host can legally declare itself the passive one. width/height are CSS pixels; dpr is separate. The runtime additionally reads a runtimeHost.insets that this interface does not declare and no host supplies.

name: runtimeListen
summary: The runtime’s only sanctioned way to add a DOM listener: it registers the handler and pushes its remover onto runtimeUnsubscribers, which destroy() drains.
detail: It no-ops on a target without addEventListener, which is what lets the same code run against the harnesses stub DOM. A raw addEventListener anywhere in runtime.js is a leak by construction. The account panel re-registers listeners on every acRender, so the disposer array grows with panel use until destroy.

name: runtimePause
summary: Freezes a live run even during the pause button’s anti-farming cooldown by zeroing PAUSE.cool while preserving PAUSE.at; otherwise it just silences audio, and it always drops held input.

name: runtimeRender
summary: Counts a frame, saves Phaser’s incoming 2D transform/alpha/composite, draws inside try/finally, and restores all three even when draw() throws.
detail: The first exception is stored on window.__drawErr rather than rethrown, and the catch resets the transform to DPR scale with source-over at alpha 1 so a broken frame cannot corrupt the next one. enginecheck asserts __drawErr is null after its run.

name: runtimeResume
summary: Unpauses if paused, otherwise re-unlocks audio and abandons the in-flight music section; contracted and exported but no shell code calls it.
detail: CosmoScene wires the native bridge resume callback to resizeToWindow instead, because returning from the background must leave the pause screen visible rather than resume a live run. Do not "fix" the apparent omission without reading docs/invariants.md.

name: runtimeSnapshot
summary: Returns a copied view of game state — cloned menuRects and introSkipRect, plus GPU background and reward blocks — and build and destroyed fields that GameSnapshot does not declare.

name: runtimeStep
summary: Converts Phaser’s delta in milliseconds to seconds, clamps it to 0.05s, rebuilds sprites when the sky band changed, then calls update() and counts one step.

name: runtimeVisibilityChanged
summary: The runtime’s own visibility handler — unlock and end the section on show, duck the pad and drain the beat/drop queues on hide — disabled whenever the host owns lifecycle.
detail: Its guard line is the externalLifecycle switch. In production the native bridge covers the same event, so this function only runs on the harness path.

name: scenePulse(kind,duration) and sceneAccent()
summary: Starts at most one authored scene event at a time and reports its current envelope to both the sky and the arena.
detail: scenePulse refuses a duplicate or a lower-ranked kind while one is live, and calls impactRecord so the arena decoration and the sky envelope come from the same event. sceneAccent returns {kind,id,strength,tint} with strength shaped by the event age.

name: schedulePreDrop(tD)
summary: Writes the pre-drop hush automation on A.hole and BED.lp — and has no call site in the shipped file.
detail: Zero callers. Because of that MU.hushEnd and MU.lpLock are only ever 0, duckBed's hush guard never trips, and A.hole is written only by endSection's restore. The 34-line comment above it states the file's central audio rule (every duck writes its own undo) using a function that never runs.

name: skyTexture / SKY_MATERIALS
summary: Resolves a sky material texture through runtimeHost.getTexture, returning null unless the image reports non-zero natural dimensions, which is the signal to draw the procedural sky.
detail: SKY_MATERIALS pairs three sprite keys with shader samplers — fx-plasma-wisp/uNebulaMap, drift-planet/uPlanetMap, drift-ring/uRingMap — and glBindSkyMaterials uploads each one that resolves. This replaced skyArtImage over an eight-entry SKY_ART_WORLDS table of authored world images; the record id is kept because code.boundary.textures and other parts link to it.

name: skyMix()
summary: Interpolates the two neighbouring WORLDS rows into one uniform set, crossfading only over the last 20% of a world.
detail: Reads SKY.w, which skyStep copies from G.skyW. Returns arc, shape, planet, surface, tint, rim, dust, star and motion. Shared by both the GPU and the CPU sky paths so they cannot disagree about where the planet is.

name: soundImpact(kind,strength)
summary: The three-voice impact for exactly three kinds — nova, hyper and orbit — and a silent no-op for anything else.
detail: Returns immediately unless kind is nova, hyper or orbit. Ducks the bed, then plays a sub, a body and (for nova/hyper) a filtered noise sweep through A.world. Called from the hypernova pickup, the nova pickup and the milestone orbit payout.

name: spawnSpike()
summary: Places one formation, trying eighteen times with relaxing clearance and downgrading rather than shipping a trap.
detail: Called from update on the spike timer. Gates and sliding gates downgrade to a single when reverseEscape fails; the saucer skips placement entirely. firstMeet is called only at a success site, and the unseen-type 1.6x telegraph is computed before the lesson stamps the seen bit.

name: startGame()
summary: Starts a run or advances a level; `carried` (a non-zero G.carryScore) is what distinguishes the two.
detail: Five call sites. Fields inside if(!carried) are per-run; everything else is per-level, which matches the scale telemetry's `seconds` uses. It silently pre-climbs G.tier and G.nRings for a level-2+ start so no banner fires over the card.

name: startStarfall() and tickStarfall(dt)
summary: Opens the Starfall reward — a nova blast, three timed waves of guaranteed stars, and invulnerability for its whole length.
detail: startStarfall refuses outside play, during the intro, inside a black hole, or while one is already running. tickStarfall runs from updateOrbMotion and re-asserts G.invuln every frame so a black-hole detour cannot eat the earned safety. The result summary lands in G.starfallResult.

name: subF(f)
summary: Octave-doubles any frequency below 40 Hz so a low level key keeps its pitch class and still moves air on a phone.
detail: Signature subF(f) -> number. Guards every dedicated sub voice: the drop boom, the payoff floor, the braam and the layer-three drone. Without it level 6's roots fall to 23-31 Hz, which reproduces on nothing the game ships to.

name: sweptHit(target,tol)
summary: Tests whether the comet crossed an angle at any point during this frame, not just where it ended up.
detail: Uses G.sweep, G.prevAngle and G.dir. Every collision and pickup in the game goes through it, which is what stops tunnelling on a large screen or after a dropped frame.

name: TIERS
summary: The thirteen-rung unlock ladder: dl threshold, formation type, banner name, lesson sub and optional ring count.
detail: Read by tierIndex, featuredTier, pickType, tierLabel, the ratchet in update and the derived T_VOICE/T_SKY lookups. Rows with type:null announce a ring or the end of teaching and carry no formation. smoke.mjs pins the last rung to the last level's floor.

name: toggleMute()
summary: Gates A.out, persists the choice, prints an acknowledgement, and ends any live section — but never stops the clock.
detail: Called from the mute rect, the M key and nothing else. Muting mid-section ends it rather than letting it run out against a silent bus. A silent run keeps the groove, the score from it, the drop and the visual beat.

name: update(dt)
summary: The simulation frame. The one return inside frozen() is the entire pause mechanism.
detail: Called from runtimeStep with dt clamped to 0.05 s. G.t+=dt sits at 7752, below the freeze gate; sdt (8161) is the further-scaled delta the world moves on, and pdt (7815) is the presentation delta particles and the sky ride.

name: updateSpikes(sdt,lethal)
summary: Advances every shard and is the game's only lethal-contact site.
detail: lethal=false is used by the menu demo and the death screen so shards still animate without being able to kill. labGhost() short-circuits the whole lethal branch, so nothing downstream fires — no shield, no pip, no popup, no death.

name: WORLDS
summary: Eight procedural destinations: position, arc shape, planet placement, surface materials and three colour vectors each.
detail: Order is the journey order and is load-bearing — LEVEL_HOME is a floor against a journey that never goes backwards, so a level home that sits behind an earlier one is dead. Interpolated by skyMix and uploaded as uArc/uShape/uPlanet/uSurface/uTint/uRim/uDust.

name: the DOM account panel
summary: The only part of the runtime that touches real DOM nodes — four views behind one door, guarded so a stubbed document cannot throw.
detail: Owns acEl/acH/acSub/acBody (4028), acOn, AC_DOM (4043), esc (4050), num, openAccount/closeAccount, acRender (4080-4204) and the action helpers. AC_DOM is the feature gate: every harness but one runs this file against a stubbed DOM. esc() is the only thing between a stranger's twelve-character display name and script execution on another player's device. The panel exists only on the title screen and keyDown returns early while it is open.

name: say, sayNow and annPump
summary: One announcement queue with priority and a shelf life, so six systems cannot overwrite each other's single line.
